video_title: Kidd Out As Mavs’ Coach: Where Will Dallas Go From Here?

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Bad signs leading to Jason Kidd's departure from Mavericks
quotes.excerpt: Jason Kidd was not aware Masai Ujiri was being hired.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Jason Kidd was not aware Masai Ujiri was being hired.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: That was a bad sign.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: After Jason Kidd, by the way, tried to move up to the front office and become the President of Basketball Operations.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Bad sign one.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Jason Kidd knew months in advance that wasn't going to happen. It's not like he was surprised he didn't get the job.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Correct me if I'm wrong on this, McMahon. Bad sign part one, ready? Jason Kidd was not aware that Masai Ujiri was being hired to be the team president.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Pretty bad sign.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Bad sign number two, maybe not at all of them, but I heard that when the Mavericks had meetings with potential draft picks last week in Chicago, that Jason Kidd wasn't always in the room.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Hmm. I would say that's not a great sign.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Considering they have a lottery pick and it's pretty important.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri's clean slate approach for the Mavericks
quotes.excerpt: Masai Ujiri is in charge, he is there, he is a huge personality, he is a fresh face.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: To me, this all goes back to not the head-to-toe comment from Masai at his press conference, but when Masai talked about the Luka Doncic trade. What did he say about the Luka Doncic trade? That is now in the past, we are done talking about the Luka Doncic trade and we are looking forward as an organization and we're moving past it.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: What they're trying to do is clean house of anybody who had any level of involvement in that.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: That's what I was getting to. This is Masai Ujiri is in charge, he is there, he is a huge personality, he is a fresh face and he is completely starting over with the Mavs.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Clean slate is the messaging from the Mavericks.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: 100%. And that's what this is. We've got Cooper Flag, we're going to have another, you got the ninth pick in this draft, they're going to get another really interesting young player in the draft. We'll see what they do with Kyrie Irving, whether they trade him or not. See if they get Derek Lively healthy. They're moving forward, build around Cooper Flag and it's forward-looking and forward-facing and we're not thinking about the Luka trade anymore.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: They're trying to move past the Luka trade.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: That's right. We're getting past all this stuff. If Jason Kidd was still coaching the team, you'd still be thinking about the Luka trade. It'd be part of the whole thing. And it's now, it's all about what's going on with Cooper, where are the Mavs going from here?

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri's track record of hiring undiscovered coaching talent
quotes.excerpt: Masai's track record is not necessarily swinging for big names. It's trying to find the next great coach.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: I would say a couple things. There is like, there's rumors flying around and I'm not going to say, there's like a big-name college coach is being rumored. Masai's track record is not necessarily swinging for big names. It's trying to find the next great coach. He likes discoveries.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Well, that's what, when he hired Nick Nurse.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: He's hired two coaches. He's hired Nick Nurse and he's hired Darko Rajakovic. Those are the two coaches he's hired.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Right. And with Darko, the other guys, like some other candidates there were Charles Lee, who is now a first-time head coach in Charlotte, doing a really good job. Chris Johnson, who is now a first-time head coach in San Antonio, doing a really good job. It wasn't a bunch of like big-name coaches is my point. Now, I don't know which direction Masai is going to go. Patrick Dumont, his MO is the exact opposite. Let me get the biggest, most proven name with the best resume possible. Rick Welts as a CEO, Masai Ujiri. But this is going to be Masai's search. Mike Schmitz, a former colleague, who's now the Mavs GM, will be part of that process. And then Dumont will be kept abreast of things, but not directly involved until they get it down to the last batch of finalists.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Patrick Dumont's willingness to pay Jason Kidd's remaining contract
quotes.excerpt: There are not many owners that would say I'm going to eat 40 plus million dollars.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: And by the way, I give credit to Patrick Dumont because as has been reported, Jason Kidd had a contract I believe through 2030 and was owed north of $40 million. And that's a lot of money to eat, especially when you extended him a year ago.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: He got two extensions from Patrick Dumont. One during the Finals run and then again last year.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: So for Masai Ujiri to go to Patrick Dumont and say, 'Hey, listen, I want to make a coaching change.' There are not many owners that would say, 'I'm going to eat 40 plus million dollars.' They would say, 'Hey, give this a year and see how it goes first because I don't want to pay that much money.' So, full credit to him for hiring Masai Ujiri and saying, 'Hey, you're going to run the team and we're going to let you do it how you want to do it and if that means we got to spend a lot of money, then so be it.'

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: And what I would say is Masai didn't necessarily go to Dumont and say, 'Hey, I want to make a change.' Patrick Dumont hired Masai Ujiri and said, 'Listen, don't worry about the money with Jason Kidd. If you want to move on from him, you're fully authorized to make that decision.'
